answer: A slashable stake plus peer attestation makes each agent identity expensive to counterfeit. To earn rewards an agent locks a bond and collects vouchers from distinct, already-staked peers. One adversary can mint endless keys but cannot mint independent guarantors, so every fake node needs fresh capital and bought trust. Duplicates found sharing funding or vouchers forfeit their bond, so a Sybil ripple costs real money per head. Honest agents climb a terrace of earned reputation, while attackers never reach the payout horizon because required stake outruns any gain.
